scope: W5B off-host source audit and portable fixture; no Linux/x86 VM admission or AMD measurement
result: The proposed Java/Jedis benchmark needs trusted clock, entropy, CPU profile and executable-code controls. CPUID RNG masking, fixed RNG rewrite sites and UseFastUnorderedTimeStamps=false do not establish those controls.

inputs.benchmark_profile: research/benchmarks/profile.json:redis-jedis-v1-100ops (W4 performance profile proposed; JDK/Jedis pins selected by coordinator)
inputs.pin_authority: Coordinator selected Jedis5.2.0 and jdk21 from unchanged research/env/flake.lock; W4 owns classpath lock; no competing selection

linux_jdk21.qualification: Read-only Nix evaluation; selected upstream files downloaded and hashed. Final patched Linux closure, libjvm and guest launch were not built or audited here.

portable_fixture.qualification: Cached shared-lock JDK; differs from Linux/x86 guest runtime

inputs.source_reference_format: Paths below are upstream files at the exact tag; lines are 1-based in downloaded files. Source manifest supplies exact raw URLs and SHA256.

findings.result: Linux System.nanoTime calls CLOCK_MONOTONIC and currentTimeMillis/UTC call CLOCK_REALTIME through clock_gettime. C2 time intrinsics target those native functions. This does not prove libc/vDSO reads are mediated.
findings.required_control: World-owned realtime, monotonic and CPU accounting, consistent timer/timeout semantics and restored epochs; audit guest libc/vDSO/clocksource as well as syscall results. Include native sockets, sleeps and JVM condition waits.

findings.result: When Rdtsc::initialize is reached, it initializes hardware before checking flag ergonomics: initialize_elapsed_counter -> initialize_frequency -> set_epoch -> raw os::rdtsc. With invariant TSC hidden it can additionally calibrate using sleep and more RDTSC. False disables selection of the fast counter after that work; it is not an early no-RDTSC guard.
findings.required_control: Either audit and patch an early JDK guard before hardware initialization, or mediate every reached direct TSC path including startup/calibration and guest vDSO. A guard proposal is unimplemented. The flag requires -XX:+UnlockExperimentalVMOptions before -XX:-UseFastUnorderedTimeStamps.
findings.qualification: Exact source control-flow finding; Linux startup reachability/fault handling and all machine-code sites remain unmeasured. Portable ARM launch verifies option syntax only.

findings.result: HotSpot emits executable CPUID/XGETBV probing stubs and caches features used for instruction selection/ergonomics. Compilation policy consumes monotonic time. JIT code pages are created after static image admission.
findings.required_control: Pin a coherent complete CPU/topology/frequency/XCR0/XSAVE profile before boot/warmup and retain it across restore. Close native classpath/agents/JNI and dynamic code loading. Define executable-page creation, mutation and alias coverage for trusted JIT/stubs; static opcode manifests do not cover arbitrary generated code.
findings.qualification: No claim that ordinary Java time intrinsics themselves emit RDTSC or that this source subset excludes other RNG/TSC instructions. No general JIT/executable mapping admission mechanism implemented.

findings.result: SUN default PRNG selection depends on provider/source configuration and availability. NativePRNG MIXED chooses configured seed file or /dev/random, takes next bytes from /dev/urandom, and combines provider PRNG state. Its reusable buffer expiry is wall-time dependent (100ms). SeedGenerator can use a URL source or fall back to a timing/thread collector.
findings.required_control: Control kernel entropy from early boot and retain complete kernel/provider state. Pin installed java.security, provider order, EGD/DRBG options and entropy endpoints; rule out unsupported fallback sources. Record selected algorithm/provider from the actual guest, without treating one sample as coverage. Changing EGD alone does not route all NativePRNG next bytes to that seed file.

findings.result: A warm snapshot inherits Random, per-thread ThreadLocalRandom, provider buffers and PRNG state. A new simulator seed controls future world inputs only under an explicit contract; it does not inherently reset these objects. SecureRandom.setSeed supplements existing seed; ThreadLocalRandom.setSeed is unsupported. Default Random and ThreadLocalRandom can initially depend on clocks.
findings.required_control: Keep W4's explicit stateless SplitMix64 workload seed as a separate pinned input. If a run should change workload seed after warm restore, supply it at START through a reviewed explicit application reset/init contract. State whether warm snapshot identity fixes inherited entropy, or implement a complete reseed policy; kernel reseeding alone is incomplete.
findings.qualification: Portable serialized-Random negative demonstrates object-state semantics, not a VM restore or provider-cache reseed implementation.

findings.result: Jedis resolves all addresses and calls Collections.shuffle when more than one is returned. That overload uses a static default Random. Socket connect/read timeouts and TCP keepalive also need guest timer/network semantics.
findings.required_control: Use one exact IPv4 literal per peer and plain non-TLS sockets in the proposed narrow profile; pin socket factory, mapper, no-retry connection behavior and timeouts. Additional pools, cluster discovery, DNS, TLS or custom providers require further audit. Freeze all runtime/transitive classpath hashes from W4.

findings.result: Safepoint polls/handshakes are JVM state and tiered compilation/GC continue in guest threads. Observed safepoints do not establish simulator stop boundaries or controller mediation.
findings.required_control: Use W4's pinned heap/G1/compiler/CPU flags and capture all JVM/kernel threads, code cache, compiler queues/counters, GC state, polling/handshake state, sockets and clocks in full VM/world restore. Continue to use W5a/W3 boundary and state contracts; no new yield/preemption hooks proposed here.

checks: Two fresh seed42 payloads equal; seed43 differs
Two self-checks byte-identical; serialized warmed Random ignores changed external seed property
All three observe logs contain probe JIT compilation, G1 collection and safepoints
limits: 32MiB diagnostic heap differs from W4 128MiB benchmark heap
Native clocks, SecureRandom and ThreadLocalRandom observer fields are intentionally noncanonical
No Linux/x86, AMD, seeded CRNG, full VM snapshot, executable-page mediation or performance acceptance

next_linux_checks_for_coordinator: Freeze W4 Linux image/runtime/classpath/flags and record effective flags, CPU leaves/XCR0, installed security configuration and provider selection before START snapshot.

Exercise cold startup, warmup and post-restore Java time/CPU reads, timed socket waits, GC and recompilation under W2's selected clock/TSC policy. Verify direct-TSC policy with omitted-control negative; include vDSO/native libraries and generated code coverage.

Repeat identical warm snapshot and seed under fresh host processes with W3 witnesses. Vary world entropy seed separately from workload seed and assert the documented inherited-state versus future-input behavior.
Keep Java/JIT admission open until executable-code scope and direct RNG/TSC bypass controls have actual guest evidence. Existing fixed fixtures and portable Java checks cannot close that gate.
